meta.what: Twice-told stories (doublets) in the Pentateuch with verse ranges and source attribution
meta.attribution_rule: csv_dominant/csv_share are measured from this repo's per-verse CSVs (Wikiversity color-coded DH edition, Friedman tradition) and are what the visualization draws; 'conventional' records the classical assignment and 'discrepancy' is noted where they differ.
sources: Richard Elliott Friedman, Who Wrote the Bible? (1987) and The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)
Julius Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)
Wikipedia: Wife-sister narratives in the Book of Genesis (source-criticism section)
Wikiversity: Bible, English, King James, According to the documentary hypothesis (the repo's upstream text)

doublets.title: Two creations
doublets.note: A seven-day cosmic creation by 'God', then a garden story where 'the LORD' forms man from dust before any plants.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Two family lines from Adam
doublets.note: Cain's line of city-builders and musicians, then the Book of Generations' ten-generation line through Seth.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: The flood: two commands to board
doublets.note: God orders two of every animal into the ark; the LORD orders seven pairs of the clean ones. Both survive, interleaved.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Two covenants with Abraham
doublets.note: A smoking firepot passes between split carcasses at sunset; later God Almighty gives the covenant of circumcision.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional J vs CSV-dominant E; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Hagar driven out twice
doublets.note: Pregnant Hagar flees Sarai's harshness to a desert spring; years later Abraham expels her and the boy Ishmael.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Wife passed off as sister (Egypt / Gerar)
doublets.note: Abram tells Pharaoh that Sarai is his sister; Abraham later plays the same trick on King Abimelech of Gerar.
doublets.basis: Wikipedia, 'Wife-sister narratives in the Book of Genesis' (source-criticism section)

doublets.title: Wife passed off as sister (Gerar, twice)
doublets.note: Abraham deceives Abimelech about Sarah; a generation later Isaac deceives an Abimelech of Gerar about Rebekah.
doublets.basis: Wikipedia, 'Wife-sister narratives in the Book of Genesis' (source-criticism section)

doublets.title: Beersheba named twice
doublets.note: Abraham swears an oath with Abimelech over a well and names Beersheba; Isaac's servants re-enact it a generation later.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional E vs CSV-dominant J; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Bethel consecrated twice
doublets.note: Jacob dreams of the ladder and names Bethel on his way out; God appears again to name it when he returns.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Jacob renamed Israel twice
doublets.note: A night wrestler at Peniel renames Jacob; God Almighty repeats the renaming at Bethel.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Two reasons Jacob leaves home
doublets.note: Rebekah sends Jacob away to escape Esau's murder plot; in the next breath he is sent to find a proper wife.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Joseph sold twice over
doublets.note: Judah persuades his brothers to sell Joseph to Ishmaelites; Midianites pull him from the pit in the seam of the same scene.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional E vs CSV-dominant J; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: The name of God revealed twice
doublets.note: At the burning bush God discloses the name; in Egypt God tells Moses that Abraham knew him only as God Almighty.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Passover legislated twice
doublets.note: Precise Priestly statute (lamb per household, four-day wait), then the elders told to slay it with hyssop and blood.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional J vs CSV-dominant P; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Manna and quail, twice
doublets.note: Bread from heaven with Sabbath rules in the wilderness of Sin; later the people crave meat and quail bury the camp.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Water from the rock, twice
doublets.note: Moses strikes the rock at Massah-Meribah; at Meribah again he strikes twice and is barred from the land for it.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional E vs CSV-dominant J; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Judges appointed twice
doublets.note: Jethro tells Moses to delegate justice; Deuteronomy has Moses recall deciding it himself.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: The mountain of God, seen twice
doublets.note: Thunder, fire and trumpet at Sinai; Deuteronomy retells the day the mountain burned, at Horeb.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

doublets.title: The two Decalogues
doublets.note: The Ten Commandments spoken at Sinai and repeated, with a different Sabbath rationale, on the plains of Moab.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: The 'ritual decalogue'
doublets.note: After the calf, the LORD rewrites the tablets - but dictates a different, festival-centred list of commands.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

halves.discrepancy: conventional J vs CSV-dominant R; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Two early festival calendars
doublets.note: The Covenant Code's three pilgrim feasts, and the near-identical list in the rewritten tablets.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

halves.discrepancy: conventional J vs CSV-dominant R; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: The golden calf, told twice
doublets.note: Aaron casts the calf and Moses shatters the tablets; Deuteronomy retells the whole scandal in Moses' own voice.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Two full festival calendars
doublets.note: Leviticus' priestly liturgical year, and Deuteronomy's pilgrim calendar centred on 'the place the LORD shall choose'.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

doublets.title: Clean and unclean animals, twice
doublets.note: Two dietary law codes: Leviticus' taxonomy of the clean and unclean, repeated with variations in Deuteronomy.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

doublets.title: Hebrew slave release, twice
doublets.note: The Covenant Code frees a male slave in year seven; Deuteronomy repeats the law and adds the sister explicitly.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

doublets.title: The spies, told twice
doublets.note: Twelve scouts and the forty-year sentence in Numbers; Deuteronomy retells the rebellion at Kadesh-barnea.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

doublets.title: Two rebellions woven into one
doublets.note: Korah's Levite mutiny over priesthood and the Dathan-Abiram revolt over Moses' rule share one chapter.
doublets.basis: Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (2003)

halves.discrepancy: conventional J vs CSV-dominant E; trusting the CSV

doublets.title: Tithes assigned twice
doublets.note: Numbers gives every tithe to the Levites; Deuteronomy has the farmer eat it before the LORD, or its money-equivalent.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)

doublets.title: Cities of refuge, twice
doublets.note: Six asylum cities for accidental killers in Numbers; Deuteronomy commands three, with the same blood-avenger logic.
doublets.basis: Wellhausen, Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1883)
